_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Designing and auditing the multi-graph context architecture of an AI-coding workspace: skill graph, document routing…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "we have ~300 skills but the agent never finds half of them — what's the diagnostic frame?"
cases.context: The agent has access to the context-graph skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is context-graph the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes context-graph as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against skill-router, skill-infrastructure, skill-scaffold
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the context-graph workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore context-graph
Does not route to skill-router, skill-infrastructure, skill-scaffold when the context-graph scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence

cases.scenario: A user asks: "scaffold a new SKILL.md from a template"
cases.context: This is a boundary test. The skill should avoid false-positive activation and route to the better owner when appropriate.
cases.question: Should context-graph be applied here? If not, what should happen instead?
expected_flags: Recognizes the request is outside context-graph's ownership
Routes the work to skill-router or asks for the missing owner instead of forcing this skill
Preserves any real issue in the request without applying context-graph terminology incorrectly
expected_fix_hints: Decline to apply context-graph as the primary skill
Name the better owner or the boundary reason
Offer only a narrow handoff if context-graph has a secondary support role
absent_signals: Does not claim context-graph should own the request
Does not use context-graph's framework to solve an explicitly excluded problem
Does not suppress the correct adjacent owner
